title: Shared TextField, TextInput, Select and SelectField components
summary: Almost every text box and dropdown in Seed Bible now uses one shared design: an outlined box with a bold label above it, a colored border while you type, a red border when something is wrong, and the same arrow on every dropdown. About 60 boxes across Settings, sign-in, profile, playlists, customization, reading plans, saves, sharing, the Books selector and some extensions moved onto it. Nothing should work differently: these tests check that each moved box still looks right, takes typing, and saves what it did before.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** button above, in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the new version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser, so it can show an older version. Do a hard refresh once: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. A private/incognito window also gives a clean start.

setup.title: What every box should look like
setup.body: Through this plan, "the shared look" means: a box with a thin grey outline and rounded corners; a bold label above it (where it has one); while you type in it, the outline turns the app's main color and gets slightly thicker, all the way round and not cut off at any edge; dropdowns have a small arrow at the right. Note any box that looks different from its neighbors.

setup.title: Light and dark
setup.body: Do the tests in the theme you normally use. If you have time, repeat a few in the other theme (switch it in **Settings**) and check the boxes are still easy to see.

tests.title: The sign-in boxes look right and still sign you in
steps: Make sure you're signed out (use a private/incognito window if needed).
Choose **Sign in** (or the profile button) to open the sign-in window.
Click in the email box (placeholder **Enter your email address**) and type your email address.
Continue, then type the code from your email into the code box (**Enter login code here**) and continue.
expected: Both boxes have the shared look, and the outline turns the main color while you type.
The code you type appears in the code box and signs you in.

tests.title: Edit profile: boxes save and the description shows a character count
steps: Open your profile and choose **Edit profile**.
Look at **Profile name**, **Location** and **Description**.
Type `Testing the count` into **Description**.
Change **Location** to `Austin, TX`, then save.
expected: Each box has a bold label above it and the shared look.
Under **Description** a count like `17/300` updates as you type.
After saving, your profile shows the new location and description.

tests.title: Optional: a screen reader reads the box names
tests.why: Many boxes used to have only grey placeholder text, so screen readers had no name for them.
steps: Turn on your screen reader: **VoiceOver** on Mac (Cmd+F5), or **Narrator** on Windows (Ctrl+Windows key+Enter).
Open **Edit profile** and press **Tab** to move into each box.
Turn the screen reader off again with the same keys.
expected: Each box is read out with its name ("Profile name", "Location", "Description"), and the description's count is read as "… of 300 characters".

tests.title: Each Settings dropdown changes only its own setting
steps: Open **Settings**.
Change **Scripture Font** to a different font and look at the Bible text.
Change **UI size** and see the app's buttons and text change size; then set it back.
Change **Book order**, open the Books list, and check the order changed; then set it back.
Open **Verse Selection Effects** and **Viewing areas** and pick a different option in each.
expected: Every dropdown has a bold label above it, the shared outline and the same arrow at the right.
Clicking a dropdown opens the browser's normal list of choices.
Each change applies straight away, and only that setting changes.

tests.title: Keyboard focus shows a ring inside the border
steps: In **Settings**, press **Tab** repeatedly until a dropdown is selected.
Keep pressing **Tab** past the **Language** picker.
expected: The selected dropdown's outline turns the main color, drawn inside the box, with no part of it cut off at the window's edge.
The **Language** picker has the same box look as the other dropdowns, with a **Language** label.

tests.title: Extensions: the "add from a link" box and an extension's settings
steps: In **Settings**, open **Extensions**.
Choose **Add from a link** and type `https://example.com` into the **Link** box. Don't add anything.
Close that, then open the settings of any installed extension that has settings (for example a text, number or dropdown option).
Change one value, then use **Reset**.
expected: The **Link** box has the shared look and its colored outline isn't clipped at the edges.
The extension's settings boxes and dropdowns have the shared look, take your change, and go back to their default on **Reset**.

setup.title: Have a playlist to edit
setup.body: Signed in. Open **Playlists** and choose **Create** to make a new playlist (or open one you already made) so you're in the playlist editor.

tests.title: A bad link is flagged, then clears when fixed
steps: In the playlist editor, add a step and choose the link (or video) type.
Type `not a link` into the link box and try to add it.
Change the text to `https://example.com` and add it.
expected: With `not a link`, the box's border turns red and **Enter a valid URL** appears under it.
As soon as you edit the text the red border and message go away, and the valid link is added.

tests.title: Step boxes match the playlist editor's colors
steps: Add a note step and a question step.
Type in their **Title**, **Note**, **Question** and **Answer** boxes.
Open a step's details sheet (on a phone-width window it opens from the bottom).
expected: The boxes fit the playlist editor's own colors and font, with labels above them, both inside the step cards and in the details sheet.
What you type is kept after closing and reopening the step.

sections.title: Other screens that moved onto the shared boxes

tests.title: Reading plan editor: naming a plan
steps: Open the reading plans screen and start a new plan.
At **Name your plan**, type `My test plan` and continue to save it.
expected: The name box has the shared look, takes the typing, and the plan is saved with that name.

tests.title: Saves: create and rename a folder
steps: Save any verse or note, and in the save picker create a new folder named `Test folder`.
Open **Saves**, open that folder's menu and choose **Rename**.
Change the name to `Renamed folder` and press **Enter**.
Choose **Rename** again, type something different, and press **Escape**.
expected: The **Folder name** box has the shared look.
When renaming, the box starts with the current name; **Enter** saves `Renamed folder`, and **Escape** leaves it unchanged.

tests.title: Bookmark name, Add a friend, and the share window
steps: Add a bookmark and type a name into its name box.
Open **Add a friend** and type into its box (you don't need to send anything).
Open the share window for a passage, change the **Theme** dropdown, and look at the **Embed code** box.
Try typing into the **Embed code** box, then select its text and copy it.
expected: Each box has the shared look and takes typing.
The **Theme** dropdown has a label and changes the embed code.
The **Embed code** can be selected and copied but not typed into.

tests.title: Colour picker: the "#" stays at the left of the hex box
steps: Open the customization editor (where you change the app's colors) and open a color picker.
Click the **Hex color** box and type `3366cc`.
expected: A `#` stays fixed at the left of the box, the color changes to blue, and the box has the shared look.

tests.title: Books selector: testament dropdown and custom translation link
steps: Open the Books selector.
Look at the **Testament** dropdown next to the translation button and search box, and choose **Old Testament**.
Open the translation list and find the box for a custom translation link (**Enter URL**) with its **Import** button.
expected: The **Testament** dropdown is the same height and filled style as the translation button and search box beside it, and choosing **Old Testament** shows only Old Testament books.
The **Enter URL** box leaves room for **Import**; the button isn't covered or pushed off the edge.

tests.title: Customization editor: item form and name boxes
steps: In the customization editor, open the name box, a variant's name box and the font box.
Open a content library and add an item, looking at its form, its category dropdown, and the website import box.
expected: All these labels and boxes look the same as each other and as the rest of the app.

setup.title: Make the window phone-sized
setup.body: Use a phone, or make your browser window as narrow as it goes (about 400 pixels wide).

tests.title: Boxes fit on a narrow screen
steps: Open **Settings**, then **Edit profile**, then the playlist editor.
Tap into a few boxes and dropdowns.
expected: No box spills past the edge of the screen or makes the page scroll sideways.
On a phone, tapping a dropdown opens the phone's own picker.

sections.title: Extensions that changed
sections.intro: Only if you use these extensions; otherwise mark the tests Skip.

tests.title: Find the Verse: game creator boxes and empty-hint errors
steps: Open **Find the Verse** and create a new game.
Type a game name and a verse reference, leave the hint boxes empty, and save.
expected: The game name, reference and hint boxes have the shared look.
The empty hints get a red border, and the screen scrolls to and zooms the error as it did before.

tests.title: Twitch host: custom announcement timer
steps: Open the Twitch host settings.
Set the announcement timer dropdown to **Custom** and type `7` into the minutes box.
expected: The dropdown and minutes box look like the rest of the app (not plain browser boxes), and the custom minutes are kept.

notCovered: Areas left out of this change on purpose: the chat composer, the Question answers reply box, the annotation writing area, the Scripture margins number box, the language picker's search box, and two pill-shaped dropdowns in the customization editor.
The extension review form, which only admins can open.
The MCP (AI chat) extension's settings boxes, which need that extension set up.
The new phone-testing developer tool in this pull request, which isn't part of the app.
Which box each hint and error message is tied to for screen readers in every screen; automated tests check these.
